correctness.rationale: Minimum-degree first-force lemma forces any cardinality-degree forcing set to contain all but one neighbor of a minimum-degree vertex. For P_n^k the only minimum-degree vertices are endpoints: all 2k possible sets are valid, giving two K_k families with cross-match, bridge, or none according to n=k+2,k+3,>=k+4. For C_n^k every center has degree 2k; the n cyclic window families consist of K_(2k) with exactly one shared vertex for adjacent centers, yielding n(2k-1) configurations and connectivity. For n>=2k+4, classify exchanges by center separation 0,1,2 to count nk(2k-1)+n(2k-2)+n=n(k+1)(2k-1). Independently enumerated all candidate minimum subsets in 32 small parameter cases and token jumps; all matched. Finite checks corroborate all-parameter combinatorial proof.
